notes: Verified record. Symbols differ by page (globalfastener d / d_c / h, fasten.it d / d1 / s, shop lists Innendurchmesser / Außendurchmesser / Stärke); mapped by header text and each page's drawing. 'nominal = min' (hole) and 'nominal = max' (outside diameter) are printed by globalfastener and fasten.it; the shop lists give the nominal sizes only. M3.5 and M14 are non-preferred sizes. Rows M18, M22, M27-M36 and the limit columns stay out: only globalfastener and fasten.it print them (2 clusters).

verification.checks_done: All pages re-downloaded by the verifier with curl (browser User-Agent) on 2026-11-11 into a separate directory (HTTP 200, text/html); tables re-read with the verifier's own parser (html.parser grid with rowspan/colspan), not the researcher's scripts or raw files. Pages: globalfastener detail_232 + detail_5239, fasten.it din_en_iso_7093-1 (+ its empty iso_7093-1 page), Odoerfer list (static HTML), Keller & Kalmbach list rendered with playwright (6 result pages; 100 of its 105 articles came back as rows - 5 were served twice instead - and the filter counts cover all 105; DOM rows and the page's own JSON both read), and the DIN 9021-type pages fasteners.eu ISO/7093 + DIN/9021, schrauben-lexikon ISO_7093 + DIN_9021, boltport iso-7093. 12 rows x 3 columns = 36 cells: d1 has 4 clusters (3 for M3.5, which Odoerfer does not list), d2 and h exactly 3 (globalfastener, fasten.it, Keller & Kalmbach). No dissent among counted pages. The DIN 9021-type pages differ from the record at M5 h, M20 d1, M24 d1 and are not counted.
problems: Independence of globalfastener and fasten.it (decided: two clusters, zero slack). Their mass column is identical for all 18 sizes, including three values that do not follow from the dimensions printed beside them (M5 1.46 = the old DIN 9021 mass for h 1.2; M33 479 instead of about 360; M36 520 instead of about 522). Reasons for not merging: (1) both name the DIN edition as their source (fasten.it: 'source DIN EN ISO 7093-1, 11-2000 ... Reproduced by permission of DIN'; globalfastener keeps the mass row only on its DIN EN ISO page, not on its ISO page), so a shared mass table is what two transcriptions of that edition look like; (2) layout, symbols and column sets differ (sizes across vs down, d/d_c/h vs d/d1/s, fasten.it has no d max / h max, globalfastener prints both); (3) elsewhere in this batch the two sites disagree with each other (ISO 8735 c for d 16: 4.6 vs 4.7; ISO 8733 thread depth for d 12/16/20: 12/16/18 vs 10/12/16; DIN 939 fine-thread list), so neither is fed from the other. If the lead prefers to merge them, d2 and h fall to 2 clusters for every row and only the d1 column of 11 rows (without M3.5) would keep 3 (globalfastener+fasten.it, Keller & Kalmbach, Odoerfer) - i.e. the table would fail in practice.
d2 and h rest on exactly three clusters for all 12 rows; M3.5 rests on a single Keller & Kalmbach article, M3 on three.

Keller & Kalmbach and Odoerfer are separate shops with different attribute sets, article numbers and size ranges (K&K: M3.5 but no M18; Odoerfer: M18, M30, M36 but no M3.5), and both print the ISO 7093-1 numbers where DIN 9021 differs (K&K: M5 thickness 1, M20 hole 21, M24 hole 25; Odoerfer: M18 19, M20 21, M24 25). Where each shop's article data come from upstream (own product data or a supplier feed) cannot be seen from the pages.
Column labels: 'nominal = min' / 'nominal = max' is stated by globalfastener and fasten.it only; the two shop lists state the plain nominal dimensions (inside diameter, outside diameter, thickness).

Not counted, for the lead's information: the publisher-authorised preview service (standards.iteh.ai sample PDF, a T1-type source under app/SOURCE_RULE.md) shows the dimension table of this ISO standard; the kept values equal it. The table could be re-based on that official preview instead of T2. (ISO 7093-1:2000 preview, Tables 1 and 2: all 18 sizes with d1 nom/max, d2 nom/min, h nom/max/min; the 36 kept cells are equal.)
